output.normalized_title: auth-gateway: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker (auth-gateway)

output.classification_reasoning: The incident is rooted in a thread deadlock within the OrderFulfillmentWorker of the auth-gateway service. A deadlock is an internal application synchronization issue, not a network, authentication, database, or storage problem, matching the provided ground‑truth category of application_error. The deadlock caused a secondary telemetry spike and impacted a large user base (45,000 users) for a moderate duration (97 minutes). Resolving such concurrency bugs typically requires code analysis, thread‑dump examination, and possibly redesign of locking mechanisms, which involves multiple components and coordination but does not usually demand a full architectural overhaul. Hence the operational effort is beyond simple but does not reach the scale of a complex, multi‑service cascade, placing the apparent complexity at the Moderate level.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
Kubectl context set to production cluster
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: auth-gateway: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Historical correlation indicates recurring pattern in auth-gateway.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 5,000 users or outage >= 120 minutes.
output.justification: The incident affects 45,000 users, far exceeding the 5,000‑user threshold defined for Tier‑1 services. According to the SLA, any Tier‑1 service impact on 5,000 or more users automatically qualifies for SEV‑1, regardless of outage duration. Although the outage duration (97 minutes) is below the 120‑minute threshold, the user impact alone satisfies the SEV‑1 criteria. Therefore, the final severity level is confirmed as SEV‑1.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Context
remediation_steps.description: Confirm the operator has required IAM role or SSO access and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster.
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals production-cluster

remediation_steps.title: Quiesce Traffic and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Activate a temporary write‑freeze, route new traffic to the read‑replica, and promote it to primary to isolate the failing auth‑gateway node.
verification: Traffic annotation present on auth-gateway deployment
RDS replica status shows 'promoting' then 'available' as primary

remediation_steps.title: Execute Graceful Rolling Restart of auth‑gateway Pods
remediation_steps.description: Trigger a rolling restart to clear the deadlocked worker threads while preserving pod affinity and readiness probes.
verification: All pods report READY 1/1 and STATUS Running
No pod restarts exceed the configured maxSurge/ maxUnavailable limits

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Validate service health via synthetic checks and confirm error‑rate reduction in logs.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=auth-gateway --since=5m | grep ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_282 || true
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
Error signature ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_282 absent in last 5 minutes of logs

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: If any verification fails or service degradation persists, revert the auth-gateway deployment to the previous stable image tag and demote the promoted read‑replica back to its original role.

steps.description: Undo the rolling restart by rolling back to the previous ReplicaSet.
verification: Pods return to the prior image tag (e.g., v1.23.4)
Pod readiness mirrors pre‑restart state

steps.description: Demote the promoted read‑replica and restore the original primary database.
verification: RDS instance identifiers show original primary as writer
Replication lag returns to < 5 seconds

steps.description: Remove traffic quiesce annotation and re‑enable normal write traffic.
verification: Annotation no longer present
Write traffic resumes without errors

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations role
Rollback procedures documented in runbook RB-125
Write‑freeze policy approved by change management
